register-harvest.title: Register a harvest
register-harvest.short: Crop, quantity, quality, location and sell-by date — typed, spoken or photographed.
register-harvest.detail: A farmer lists what is ready: crop, quantity, expected quality, location, harvest date and the last day it can be sold. They can type it, speak it in their own language, add a photo, or ask a field coordinator to list it for them. A private minimum net price stays visible only to the farmer.
register-harvest.who: Farmer, or a field coordinator on their behalf

sees.0: A draft listing built from a voice note, checked before saving
sees.1: A private minimum net price only they can see

register-harvest.safeguard: The assistant asks for missing details instead of guessing them.

group-harvests.title: Check and group harvests
group-harvests.short: Compatible harvests are pooled by crop, grade, place, quantity and timing.
group-harvests.detail: MandiMate looks across neighbouring farms for harvests that belong together: the same crop and grade, close enough to share a vehicle, ready inside the same window, and together large enough for a real buyer order. Explicit rules decide what can be pooled, so incompatible produce is never mixed.
group-harvests.who: MandiMate matching rules, reviewed by coordinators

sees.0: Why a group of harvests is a promising match
sees.1: What information is still missing before a lot is buyer-ready

group-harvests.safeguard: AI explains a match; it never silently combines incompatible produce or invents supply.

buyer-offers.title: Buyers submit offers
buyer-offers.short: Price, quantity, quality standards, pickup terms and payment conditions — in writing.
buyer-offers.detail: Verified retailers, wholesalers, processors, hotels and institutional kitchens make written offers on pooled lots: price per kilogram, quantity, quality specification, pickup terms and when they will pay. Offers can be countered and negotiated inside a single thread.

sees.0: Every term in one written offer
sees.1: Counter-offers and replies in one thread

buyer-offers.safeguard: Only verified buyers can make offers on a lot.

compare-earnings.title: Compare real earnings
compare-earnings.short: Each offer becomes net money per farmer — after transport, handling, commission and waiting.
compare-earnings.detail: For every farmer in the lot, MandiMate turns each offer into estimated net proceeds: gross value minus expected rejection, their share of transport, handling, commission and the cost of waiting for payment. It sets that beside what they would net selling alone at the local mandi.

sees.0: Net beside gross, per kilogram and in total
sees.1: Which figures are confirmed, estimated or still unresolved

compare-earnings.safeguard: Prices and costs come from offers, quotes and published rates — never from an AI guess.

farmer-consent.title: Farmers review and decide
farmer-consent.short: Each farmer sees the best feasible deal and accepts or declines. No sale without consent.
farmer-consent.detail: Every farmer in the pool reviews the proposed deal in plain language — what they would take home, what is confirmed and what is still an estimate — and accepts or declines. A farmer who declines simply leaves the lot; nobody can sell their produce for them.

sees.1: Accept or decline, with the reason recorded

farmer-consent.safeguard: No sale goes ahead without each farmer’s explicit consent.

transport-pickup.title: Coordinate transport and pickup
transport-pickup.short: One vehicle, a planned route and a pickup sequence across the pooled farms.
transport-pickup.detail: MandiMate plans collection points, picks a vehicle that fits the lot, orders the pickups along one route and invites transporters to quote. Transport is shared by weight, so a 200 kg harvest pays for 200 kg of the truck — not the whole trip.

sees.1: Your share of transport, split by weight

transport-pickup.safeguard: Logistics are costed before a deal is recommended, so transport cannot quietly eat the margin.

delivery-quality.title: Deliver and check quality
delivery-quality.short: Delivered weight, grade, shortages and rejections are recorded against each farmer.
delivery-quality.detail: At delivery the buyer records what arrived: weight, quality and grade, any shortage and any rejection — attributed to the farmer whose produce it was. Discrepancies are raised there and then, with photos and notes, rather than discovered at payment time.
delivery-quality.who: Buyer, with the coordinator and transporter

sees.0: Accepted and rejected quantity for your share

delivery-quality.safeguard: Final acceptance follows physical inspection, not a photo.

settlement-results.title: Settle and track results
settlement-results.short: Payment status, deductions and earnings versus selling alone — recorded for every sale.
settlement-results.detail: MandiMate tracks the settlement to each farmer: sale amount, every deduction, payment status and date. It then records what the farmer actually earned against what selling alone would have paid, so every harvest adds evidence about what really works.

sees.0: Payment status until the money arrives

settlement-results.safeguard: Every fee and deduction is shown; disputes have a clear, recorded process.

journeySection.lead: A listing app stops once a buyer is found. MandiMate keeps going — through consent, pickup, delivery and quality checks — until the money reaches the farmer and the result is recorded.

steps.title: What happens, who acts, and what protects the farmer.
steps.lead: Each step has an owner, a clear output and a rule that keeps the farmer in control. Nothing moves forward on a guess.

stop.title: Most platforms stop at step three. The farmer’s money is made in the other five.
stop.lead: Rejections at the gate, a half-empty truck, an unpaid invoice — that is where small farmers lose what a better price promised. MandiMate is built to carry the deal through to settlement and record what the farmer actually earned.

hero.title: What will you actually take home?
hero.lead: Compare selling your harvest alone at the mandi with a pooled sale through MandiMate — after rejection, transport, handling, commission and the wait for payment. Change any number; the answer updates instantly.

method.title: Six lines between the price and your pocket.
method.lead: Every figure comes from one published formula — the same one farmers see inside MandiMate. Where a real distance is unknown, we assume {{km}} km to the nearest mandi. Each line is rounded to the paisa and the net is their sum.

gross.title: Gross sale value
gross.body: Quantity × the price per kilogram. This is the number most apps stop at — and the one that tells you least about what you will take home.

rejection.title: Expected rejection
rejection.body: Produce refused at the gate or sold as waste is never paid for. Selling alone, ungraded produce is often rejected more; in a pooled lot, harvests are inspected and graded before pickup.

transport.title: Transport
transport.body: Selling alone, you hire a whole vehicle for your harvest. Pooled, one vehicle collects the lot along a planned route and the cost is split by weight. Estimates use published vehicle rates; a real deal uses the transporter’s quote.

handling.title: Handling & loading
handling.body: Hamali and unloading at a mandi is estimated at {{mandiRate}}. At a MandiMate collection point, loading and crates are estimated at {{loadingRate}}.

commission.title: Commission
commission.body: A commission agent at the mandi typically takes about {{pct}}% of the accepted value. MandiMate deals carry no commission for farmers — MandiMate charges buyers.

paymentWait.title: Cost of waiting for payment
paymentWait.body: Money that arrives in three weeks is worth less than money tomorrow. We price the wait at an informal credit rate of {{rate}}% a year, so a faster-paying buyer is properly rewarded.

vehicles.title: Vehicle rates used for estimates
vehicles.note: The smallest vehicle that fits the load is chosen; larger loads take more trips.

0.question: What is net earnings, and why does it matter more than price?
0.answer: Net earnings is what reaches the farmer after expected rejection, transport, handling, commission and the cost of waiting for payment. A buyer who quotes ₹2 more per kilogram can still leave a farmer with less if their transport, deductions or payment terms are worse.

1.question: How accurate is this calculator?
1.answer: It uses the same net-proceeds formula MandiMate uses inside the app, with published estimates for transport, handling and commission. Your real figures depend on the actual offer, transporter quote and quality inspection, which MandiMate marks as confirmed, estimated or unresolved in every deal.

2.question: Does MandiMate charge farmers a fee?
2.answer: No. MandiMate charges buyers a coordination fee per successfully sourced lot. The MandiMate fee line is ₹0 for farmers.

3.question: How is pooled transport shared between farmers?
3.answer: By weight. If your harvest is 400 kg of a 1,000 kg lot, you pay 40% of the vehicle cost for that route — not the whole trip.

4.question: What if selling alone pays more?
4.answer: Then MandiMate shows you that. A pooled deal is only worth taking when your net is better, and no sale goes ahead without your consent.

0.question: Why is MandiMate free for farmers?
0.answer: Our mission is to raise what farmers take home. Charging them would work against that, so the business is paid for by buyers, FPO subscriptions and a transparent logistics coordination fee.

1.question: Are these prices final?
1.answer: No. This is pilot pricing, subject to validation with real transactions. We will change it if it does not work for farmers, buyers or partners — and we will say so publicly.

2.question: Will fees reduce what a farmer earns?
2.answer: Any cost that touches a farmer’s sale — transport, handling, a commission — appears as its own line in their net earnings before they agree. Nothing is hidden inside the price.

3.question: Do buyers pay if a deal fails?
3.answer: No. The buyer coordination fee applies only to lots that are successfully sourced and delivered.
